documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Winter was slow at work, back to framing now. Swallowing still good, eats slowly, drinks water with meals. Heart: no racing, no passing out, climbs scaffolding fine. Taking all meds; uses a pill box. Bowels okay, PEG most days.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Regular rhythm, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, slight distension. No edema.

Plan: BMP for enalapril. Cardiology yearly visit due in May, he has the date. Continue current meds. See in September with labs and flu shot.

documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CARDIOLOGY GROUP
Date of visit: 05/14/2025

Annual follow-up, Chagas cardiomyopathy with apical aneurysm, LVEF 45% on the 2024 echo, RBBB. Asymptomatic: no palpitations, presyncope, syncope, chest pain or edema. Doing heavy construction work without limitation.

Meds: enalapril 10 mg daily, carvedilol 6.25 mg BID, omeprazole 20 mg daily, PEG PRN. NKDA.

Exam: BP and HR at goal. No JVD, regular rhythm, no murmur, clear lungs, no edema.
Primary care BMP 03/2025 reviewed: normal.

Assessment: stable Chagas cardiomyopathy, NYHA I.
Plan: no changes. Repeat echo at next yearly visit or sooner for symptoms. Return 1 year. He knows to seek care for palpitations, lightheadedness or fainting.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Doing well. Swallowing steady since the 2024 dilation, no food impaction. Weight 62.5, highest since he joined us. Cardiology in May: stable, no changes. No palpitations, chest pain, fainting, or swelling. Bowels every day or two on PEG.

Meds: enalapril 10 mg daily, carvedilol 6.25 mg BID, omeprazole 20 mg daily, PEG 17 g PRN. NKDA. No tobacco or alcohol.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Thin, well. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, mild distension, NT. No edema.

A/P
1. Chagas cardiomyopathy, NYHA I: stable on enalapril and carvedilol. CMP today.
2. Megaesophagus s/p dilation: doing well, weight up.
3. Megacolon: stable on PEG.
4. Health maintenance: CBC, lipids today. Flu and COVID given. PHQ-2 0.
5. Next visit in about a year unless something comes up; he'll call with any symptoms. Booked for September 2026.

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 84. Right bundle branch block, QRS 140 ms. Frequent unifocal premature ventricular complexes. No acute ST elevation.
reports.conclusion: Sinus rhythm with right bundle branch block and frequent premature ventricular complexes.

reports.text: PA and lateral views. Heart size normal. Mediastinal contours normal. Lungs clear without consolidation or edema. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Bones unremarkable.

Limited study in the emergency department.
Left ventricle: normal size. Apical thinning. Mild global systolic dysfunction, visual LVEF about 45%. No thrombus seen on available views.
Right ventricle: normal size and function.
Valves: no significant regurgitation.
Pericardium: no effusion.
reports.conclusion: Apical thinning with mild LV systolic dysfunction. No pericardial effusion.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT — PHYSICIAN RECORD
Arrival: 01/31/2026 14:40

CC: palpitations, lightheaded, chest discomfort on and off

HPI: 47 y/o M with chronic Chagas disease and cardiomyopathy, megaesophagus, megacolon. Since this morning feels his heart skipping and fluttering, with lightheaded spells while standing and brief episodes of chest discomfort. No syncope. Came in from home.

PMH: Chagas with cardiac and GI involvement, cardiomyopathy, megaesophagus, megacolon; colonoscopy with biopsies at age 42 found a very dilated colon after years of constipation and bloating.
Meds: enalapril 10 mg daily, carvedilol 6.25 mg BID, PEG 3350 17 g daily PRN, omeprazole 20 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family hx: denies family history of heart disease.
Social: no alcohol or drugs.

Vitals at triage: BP 110/68, HR 84, RR 16, SpO2 98% RA, T 36.8 C. Stable throughout.

Exam: alert, comfortable. Heart irregular with frequent ectopy, no murmur. No JVD, lungs clear, no edema. No signs of heart failure.

Results: high-sensitivity troponin I 4 ng/L. K 4.3, Mg 2.0, BMP otherwise normal. ECG: RBBB with frequent PVCs. CXR: normal heart size, clear lungs. Bedside/limited echo: apical thinning, mild LV systolic dysfunction.

ED course: on monitor for several hours, no sustained arrhythmia, symptoms eased. Discussed with on-call cardiology: no changes tonight, outpatient ambulatory monitor and clinic visit.

Diagnosis: palpitations with frequent PVCs in known Chagas cardiomyopathy.
Disposition: discharged home 01/31/2026 21:10. Follow up with cardiology within 1-2 weeks; monitor to be arranged by their office. Return for fainting, sustained racing heart, worsening chest pain or breathlessness.

Record faxed to primary care 02/03/2026.

documents.title: ER visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hello, I want to tell you I went to the emergency on Saturday because my heart was skipping a lot. They said the extra beats are from the Chagas and I need a monitor. Cardiology put the monitor on today. Do I need to come see you too?

documents.title: RE: ER visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Javier, thanks for letting us know. We received the ER record yesterday and the doctor read it. Cardiology is the right place for the monitor and next steps, so keep that visit. If you faint, the racing doesn't stop, or you get chest pain or trouble breathing, go back to the ER. You are booked with us in September; message anytime before that.

reports.text: Recording duration 48 hours. Underlying rhythm sinus with right bundle branch block, heart rate range 52-118 bpm, mean 71. Frequent unifocal premature ventricular complexes, burden 9%. No sustained or nonsustained ventricular tachycardia. No pauses or atrioventricular block. Patient-triggered events for palpitations correspond to PVCs.
reports.conclusion: Sinus rhythm with RBBB and frequent unifocal PVCs (9% burden). No ventricular tachycardia. Symptoms correlate with PVCs.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CARDIOLOGY GROUP
Date of visit: 02/18/2026

Seen after an ED visit on 01/31/2026 for palpitations and lightheadedness in the setting of Chagas cardiomyopathy (apical aneurysm, LVEF about 45%, RBBB). ED workup: troponin normal, electrolytes normal, frequent PVCs on ECG, echo unchanged.

48-hour monitor 02/04-02/06: sinus rhythm with RBBB, unifocal PVCs at 9% burden, no VT, no pauses; his symptoms match the PVCs.

Since the ED he still notices skipped beats a few times a day, less lightheaded. No syncope.

Meds: enalapril 10 mg daily, carvedilol 6.25 mg BID, omeprazole 20 mg daily, PEG PRN. NKDA.

Exam: BP and HR acceptable, occasional ectopic beats, no murmur, lungs clear, no edema.

Assessment: symptomatic frequent PVCs in Chagas cardiomyopathy without ventricular tachycardia.
Plan: increase carvedilol to 12.5 mg twice daily; new prescription sent to his pharmacy. Avoid stimulants and energy drinks. Repeat echo and monitor at the next visit in about 3 months. Return or ED for syncope or sustained palpitations.
